subject: Hospitality
title: Japanese Ryokan Tradition
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Japanese Ryokan Tradition.

hook.text: Japan's ryokan inns date back over 1,300 years. The oldest, Nishiyama Onsen Keiunkan, opened in 705 CE.

buildup.text: Ryokans offer tatami rooms, futon beds, kaiseki meals, and onsen baths—hospitality as a complete experience.

discovery.text: The concept of 'omotenashi'—selfless, anticipatory service—defines the ryokan. Needs are met before you ask.

twist.text: Many ryokans have been family-run for dozens of generations. The business passes to whichever child shows the most care.

climax.text: While Western hotels chased scale, ryokans perfected intimacy. Some host only a few guests at a time.

punchline.text: 1,300 years of family-run care. Hospitality as a life philosophy.

quiz.question: What is 'omotenashi' in Japanese hospitality?
options: Selfless, anticipatory service—needs met before asking
